body:
Reverting #108356 fixes the issue. CC @neonmoe
When i attempt to import in Godot 4.5 beta 6 using Blender 3.4 the operation fails and throw the errors: ``` ERROR: Blender exportation failed: faultCode 1 faultString :Converting py args to operator properties: : keyword "export_import_convert_lighting_mode" unrecognized ERROR: Error importing 'res://KennifiedPlayerModel.blend'. ```
Using Godot 4.6 beta 2 the error printed is bigger but points to the same problem: ``` ERROR: Blender import failed: Blender 3.4.0 (hash a95bf1ac01be built 2022-12-07 02:06:25) ERROR: Read blend: C:/Users/Matheus/Downloads/Godot MRP/Godot4.5BlenderImportBug/4_5_NonMono/KennifiedPlayerModel.blend ERROR: Error: Python: Traceback (most recent call last): ERROR: File "", line 9, in ERROR: File "C:\Users\Matheus\Downloads\blender-3.4.0-windows-x64\3.4\scripts\modules\bpy\ops.py", line 113, in __call__ ERROR: ret = _op_call(self.idname_py(), None, kw) ERROR: TypeError: Converting py args to operator properties: : keyword "export_import_convert_lighting_mode" unrecognized ERROR: ERROR: Error: script failed, expr: ' ERROR: import bpy, sys ERROR: opts = {'unpack_all': True,'path': 'C:/Users/Matheus/Downloads/Godot MRP/Godot4.5BlenderImportBug/4_5_NonMono/KennifiedPlayerModel.blend','gltf_options': {'filepath': 'C:/Users/Matheus/Downloads/Godot MRP/Godot4.5BlenderImportBug/4_5_NonMono/.godot/imported/KennifiedPlayerModel-1cdc0c19b60c6c3ca8d6af206899c550.gltf','export_keep_originals': True,'export_format': 'GLTF_SEPARATE','export_yup': True,'export_import_convert_lighting_mode': 'COMPAT','export_extras': True,'export_skins': True,'export_all_influences': True,'export_materials': 'EXPORT','export_cameras': True,'export_lights': True,'export_colors': False,'use_renderable': False,'use_visible': False,'export_texcoords': True,'export_normals': True,'export_tangents': True,'export_nla_strips': True,'export_frame_range': True,'export_force_sampling': True,'export_def_bones': False,'export_apply': True,},} ERROR: if bpy.app.version < (3, 0, 0): ERROR: print('Blender 3.0 or higher is required.', file=sys.stderr) ERROR: bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=opts['path']) ERROR: if opts['unpack_all']: ERROR: bpy.ops.file.unpack_all(method='USE_LOCAL') ERROR: bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(**opts['gltf_options']) ERROR: ', exiting. ERROR: . ERROR: Error importing 'res://KennifiedPlayerModel.blend'. ```
Also, using Blender 3.6 in the import path works without issues.

Does Godot have any specified versions of Blender it claims to support? 3.6 seems old enough to require to me. If older versions need to be supported anyway, we could try to reverse engineer what the problematic Blender flag does and apply the changes in the import process, but that feels hacky to me. It'd require multiplying all the imported lights' intensities by some factor (likely different between some light types).
